extracted.intended_audience: Stanford faculty across humanities, sciences, engineering, and medicine
extracted.subtask_description: Institutional guidance for Stanford faculty preparing external research proposals (federal, foundation, industry), covering sponsor targeting, proposal content priorities, pre-award processes, and university-specific resources and expectations. Emphasizes what wins, common SPO pre-submission catches, foundation strategy, academic voice, and timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target appropriate funding source (federal/foundation/industry)
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose a sponsor type aligned with the project's disciplinary fit (NIH, NSF, DoD/DOE, major foundations, industry gifts/consortia).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match the project's scope and audience: NIH for biomedical, NSF for basic sciences/engineering/CS, DOE for energy/SLAC-linked work, DARPA/DoD for defense-relevant engineering/CS; foundations (Gates, HHMI, Wellcome, Sloan, Packard, Simons, etc.) for mission-aligned projects; industry for tech-adjacent applied work or licensing potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong Specific Aims with clear hypothesis
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific Aims page should be compelling and state a clear hypothesis or central goal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SPO highlights 'Strong Specific Aims with clear hypothesis' as a primary success factor. Use the Specific Aims to communicate importance, objectives, and expected outcomes succinctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent aims (no failure cascade)
rubrics_metrics.description: Design aims so each can succeed independently; avoid aims that depend sequentially on one another failing or succeeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame aims so failure of one aim does not doom the entire proposal; reviewers look for parallel/orthogonal aims to de-risk the plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative preliminary data
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide quantitative preliminary data demonstrating feasibility and supporting key claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use rigorous quantitative results to justify approach and demonstrate capability; preliminary data strengthens likelihood of funding, especially for experimental proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit rigor language
rubrics_metrics.description: Address scientific rigor and reproducibility explicitly in the proposal text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include plans for replication, controls, statistical rigor, data handling, and other discipline-appropriate rigor statements (this is expected by many federal sponsors).

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage Stanford interdisciplinary centers in environment sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite and integrate relevant Stanford centers (Bio-X, Wu Tsai, HAI, Cancer Institute, etc.) to strengthen the institutional environment/evidence of collaboration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show how affiliated centers add depth to the environment and provide resources, cores, or intellectual synergies. Use centers to bolster institutional support and collaborative infrastructure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry or clinical partnerships where relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: Include industry sponsors/partners or clinical affiliations when they materially enhance translational impact or feasibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For translational or technology-transfer projects, document industry sponsorships, consortia membership, or clinical partners (Stanford Hospital, LPCH, VA Palo Alto) to strengthen impact and implementation plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Realistic budget with Stanford indirect rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare a plausible, well-justified budget that correctly applies Stanford's indirect cost rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SPO will check indirect cost calculation; ensure budgets reflect institutional rates, justify personnel and resources, and align costs with scope. Unrealistic budgets or wrong rates are common rejection drivers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address compliance requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and resolve regulatory and compliance needs early (IRB, IACUC, export controls, COI, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SPO expects compliance to be addressed prior to submission; unresolved compliance gaps are flagged in pre-submission review. Include statements of approvals or plans to obtain them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of support specific and substantive
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide targeted letters of support that speak directly to collaborations, resource commitments, or institutional backing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters should be specific about the role and resources committed; generic letters are less valuable. Multi-departmental collaborator letters and senior-leader endorsement (esp. for foundation strategy) strengthen proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation framed as feasible
rubrics_metrics.description: Present novelty clearly while showing the innovation is practical and achievable within the project scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid over-hyping; frame innovation so reviewers see novelty plus feasibility backed by preliminary data and realistic aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare and follow SPO timeline milestones
rubrics_metrics.description: Adhere to pre-award timeline: 6 weeks before deadline for budget/admin docs, 2 weeks for full draft, 1 week for final compliance/formatting, and 5 days before submission for SPO to submit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start early and respect internal deadlines; late submissions reduce SPO’s ability to catch errors. Use listed milestones as minimum lead times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use SPO pre-award services (budget, indirects, subawards, compliance, submission)
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage SPO for budget development, indirect cost calculation, subaward agreements, compliance review, and final submission via Stanford eRA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage institutional expertise to avoid administrative errors; SPO will process subawards and ensure compliance and correct submission mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid common SPO pre-submission problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure proposals do not contain budget errors, compliance gaps, subaward complications, format violations, or missing required sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this checklist during draft revisions; SPO explicitly screens for these issues and will return or block submission if present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate foundation strategies through Office of Foundation Relations
rubrics_metrics.description: Work with the Office of Foundation Relations (OFR) rather than approaching major foundations independently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OFR arranges program officer meetings, aligns strategic university-level approaches, and coordinates letters of support from senior leaders; follow OFR processes for major foundations (HHMI, Pew, Packard, Sloan, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage program officers and university leadership for foundation submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Arrange program officer meetings and secure senior leader letters when pursuing foundation funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OFR can facilitate introductions and craft strategic approaches; foundations expect university-level coordination on large/strategic proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt an academic voice: confidence without arrogance
rubrics_metrics.description: Write with assuredness while avoiding hype; cite competitors and acknowledge limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly cite related work (including competitors), position the contribution within the field, avoid exaggerated claims, and discuss limitations candidly to build credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frame interdisciplinary work genuinely
rubrics_metrics.description: When claiming interdisciplinarity, ensure the bridge between fields is real and substantiated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite relevant interdisciplinary centers, include multi-departmental collaborators, and document cross-school appointments or shared resources to demonstrate genuine interdisciplinarity rather than nominal cross-discipline phrasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasize translational potential when applicable
rubrics_metrics.description: For clinically relevant projects, highlight patient-facing potential, links to Stanford Hospital/LPCH, and technology transfer pathways.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document clinical partners, potential for translation, regulatory pathway considerations, and any industry engagement that supports implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite Stanford cores, facilities, and training programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Name and describe relevant cores (Genomics Service Center, Imaging Facility, SLAC LCLS, SUNet) and training programs to strengthen resource statements and environment sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use specific facility names and describe how they will be used; listing institutional training programs (MSTP, biosciences/engineering PhD programs, HAI fellowships) supports training and mentoring plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailor proposal themes to school-specific expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Adapt narrative and emphasis to the norms of the school: translational framing for Medicine, industry partnerships for Engineering, long-form scholarship for Humanities and Social Sciences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use school-specific examples: cite cancer/brain centers for Medicine, industry/HAI for Engineering, and Mellon/NEH/ACLs targets for Humanities; align aims, impact, and dissemination plans with school norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use institutional support services (workshops, mock reviews, Aims consultations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Participate in grant-writing workshops, mock review processes, and specific Aims page consultations offered by schools and SPO-affiliated offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These resources provide peer/mentor feedback and improve competitiveness; schedule consultations early to incorporate feedback before SPO deadlines.
